covers.quote: Accessibility is a mandatory standard for government agencies.
Accessibility is a mandatory government standard.
WCAG is a baseline accessibility standard for Australian Government content.
You need to meet the level A criteria to meet level AA.

rules.specification: This is an overarching conformance requirement, not a standalone text check. The page identifies WCAG 2.2 as current but does not enumerate its success criteria. Assessing conformance requires those external criteria and can require evidence beyond the text. Aiming above AA is aspirational, not an additional failure condition.
rules.violation_condition: Australian Government content fails an applicable WCAG level A or level AA success criterion.
when: Meeting level AA includes meeting level A criteria.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the mandatory baseline and its level A prerequisite; do not turn the aspiration to exceed AA into another check.

rules.quote: Include a page on your site that explains the extent your service or product complies with WCAG.
rules.violation_condition: An agency website lacks a page explaining the extent to which its service or product complies with WCAG.
when: Assess the agency website as a whole; the statement need not appear on every page.
rules.why: G-4: the body gives the actionable requirement and absorbs the heading; the statement is a site-level requirement.
